DDInter995.mechanism: The concomitant administration of potent CYP450 3A4 inducers may significantly reduce itraconazole and ketoconazole serum levels. The mechanism appears to be enhanced first-pass metabolism and hepatic enzyme metabolism (CYP450 3A4) of the antifungal agents. Antifungal therapy may fail.

DDInter996.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 may increase the plasma concentrations of ivabradine, which is primarily metabolized by the isoenzyme. Elevated plasma levels of ivabradine may increase the risk of excessive bradycardia and conduction disturbances.

DDInter997.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 may increase the plasma concentrations of ivacaftor, which is primarily metabolized by the isoenzyme. The interaction occurs to a greater extent when ivacaftor is administered as monotherapy than when administered in combination with lumacaftor, a potent CYP450 3A4 inducer.
